A Dutch despatch from the peace talks with Cromwell, intercepted by Thurloe’s office and printed by Birch in 1742: three cipher passages, 136 groups, figures 6–33 for letters and eight three-figure groups from a new word code. Every royalist and Commonwealth key of 1653–60 on Cryptiana fails, and a hill-climb in Dutch and French finds no reading. A matched control shows the solver would have read a letter cipher of this shape, so the system is not what it seems, or the print is corrupt. Daniel Bourdeau · posted 15 October 2026 · updated 7 November 2026 Method: not solved · Extent: text not obtained · On the map Credits · Thomas Birch (transcription) not solved At a glance Not solved · text not obtained The letter Hieronymus van Beverningh and Vande Perre, envoys of the States General negotiating with the Commonwealth, to Willem Boreel, Dutch ambassador in Paris. Westminster, 22 August / 1 September 1653. Intercepted by Thurloe’s office. Where The original is in the Bodleian, MS Rawlinson A (Thurloe papers) vol. v p. 240, not digitised. Printed by Thomas Birch, A Collection of the State Papers of John Thurloe (1742), vol. 1 p. 435, the only witness online. Satoshi Tomokiyo (Cryptiana) lists it with no known decipherment. The cipher 136 groups in three passages: figures 6–33 standing for letters (25 symbols), and eight three-figure groups (113, 117, 211, 222, 327, 329, 519, 527) for words, from a new code Boreel had sent. How it was tried Every royalist and Commonwealth key of 1653–60 on Cryptiana; a hill-climb with Dutch and French language models, one-to-one and homophonic; an alphabetical key with any shift. Then a matched control on synthetic texts of the same layout. Still open All of it. The control shows the text is long enough for the solver, so the letters are not a plain or lightly homophonic cipher of Dutch or French as modelled, or Birch’s print is corrupt.

In August 1653 the States General’s envoys in London were negotiating an end to the First Anglo-Dutch War. (This background is not from the sources and was not checked here.) Their despatch to Boreel in Paris was intercepted, copied and kept in John Thurloe’s papers, and Thomas Birch printed it in 1742 in English translation, with the cipher passages as they stood. They warn Boreel that letters addressed in English are opened, as the English assume they concern royalists, and then: “We are served with the same cypher; but hereafter to express particular words, we will rather make use of the new one, which your excellency was pleased to send unto us”. So the small figures are the old letter cipher and the three-figure groups the new word code. The three cipher passages as Birch printed them, between the clear “and do find that at Solebay” and “as was ordered by their resolution”. The three-figure groups (113, 222, 329, 527, 117, 211, 519, 327) are the new code. Image: Thomas Birch, A Collection of the State Papers of John Thurloe (1742), vol. 1 p. 435, via the Internet Archive. This despatch was one of four short pieces with no known decipherment in Birch’s volumes that Cryptiana lists together as one item. They share only the printed source, and each is in its own cipher, so each has its own page: du Gard to White, 10 June 1656 , Brussels to Copinger, 12 August 1656 and Waddall to “Vanyeare”, 22 August 1656 .

The three passages hold 136 groups, 128 of them figures 6–33 (25 distinct) and eight three-figure code groups, one per word, that break the letter runs into pieces (66, 47 and 15 letters). The low figures are a letter cipher in the plain reading: about one symbol per letter, a few to spare for homophones. The plaintext is taken to be Dutch or French; Birch’s English is his translation of the original.

Known keys. Every 1653–60 royalist and Commonwealth key that Cryptiana publishes was applied (Marshall 1656–58, Barwick–Hyde 1659–60, Stamford 1655, Butler 1656, the Charles II key intercepted in 1655, Kingston 1658, Westrope 1655, the Hague agent and Blake) and scored with English, Dutch and French quadgram models. The best scores were −4.8 to −5.4 per quadgram, against about −3.2 for real text: nothing readable. Hill-climbing. A solver on the 128 letter figures with Dutch and French quadgram models, one-to-one and homophonic, eight restarts. Its best was −4.71 per quadgram (random text about −6, real Dutch −3.0 to −3.4), with fragments such as “ormellenhebelandender” that look Dutch but do not read. An alphabetical key. A plain alphabet laid on 10–33, with any shift or reversal, was excluded.

Was the text simply too short? Synthetic ciphertexts were made in exactly this letter’s layout (66 + 47 + 15 letters, eight code groups skipped), from held-out Dutch, French and period English, and given to the same solver unchanged, 40 trials each. It read 39 of 40 Dutch, 40 of 40 French and 36 of 40 English one-to-one substitutions to 80% or better, and 26, 24 and 17 of 40 homophonic ones with 25 symbols, as here. This letter’s own best score lies below every Dutch and every French homophonic control. So a Dutch or French letter cipher of this shape, with up to two symbols per letter, would very probably have been deciphered. One of the assumptions is wrong: the figures include syllables, word signs, nulls or more homophones, or the language differs, or Birch’s transcription is corrupt.

The three passages (136 groups): not read. Blocker: no key material. The key, or another despatch of the envoys to Boreel with its decipherment, would be in the Nationaal Archief (Staten-Generaal, liassen Engeland), not online; the eight code groups need the new code Boreel sent. The original in the Rawlinson manuscripts would settle whether Birch’s figures are right. It is not digitised.

Daniel Bourdeau · posted 15 October 2026 · updated 21 October 2026 Method: not solved · Extent: text not obtained · On the map With WAINUT (solution) · Also credited · Brice Dudout (pointer to a source) not solved At a glance Not solved · text not obtained The letter Arend Willem van Reede, the Dutch Republic’s envoy in Berlin, to the Secret Committee of the States General, 24 March 1793, in Dutch: four pages of code, marked “Secret”. Where Nationaal Archief, The Hague, Staten-Generaal 1.01.02, inv. 6695; DECODE R1893 (catalogue item 231, which DECODE tags as Hungarian). The cipher A code of three-digit groups in which single digits carry one of five marks (tilde, caret, bar, dots, cross): 696 groups in 513 distinct marked forms, so a code of several thousand values. How it was tried Against the keys on DECODE that belong to the same year and office: the 1793 Fagel key bundle (R2846, R2848, R2850, R2851) and the deciphered control R2243; and against the Grand Chiffre of van Reede’s earlier despatches. Why it resists None of the keys fits, and the letter alone is too short to rebuild a code this large. A code rebuilt from Van Reede’s other secret despatches (below) gives a partial decode, too uncertain to count as a reading. Credit WAINUT rebuilt the code from 44 cipher and clear-copy pairs and decoded the letter in part ( pull request #66 , 21 October 2026); recorded as a proposal. What would finish it The Secret Committee’s key, or a deciphered copy from the States General’s secret files (NA 1.01.02). Other ciphers Van Reede’s despatches of 1787–88 to Van de Spiegel are in William V’s Grand Chiffre and are deciphered on their own page . R1893, first page: “Secret”, the dates 24 March and 5 April in the margin, and the first rows of marked three-digit groups. Image: Nationaal Archief, The Hague, Staten-Generaal 1.01.02 inv. 6695, first page, via DECODE R1893. Contributed, 21 October 2026: a partial decode, recorded as a proposal. WAINUT , a Dutch AI company, found 44 of Van Reede’s secret despatches of 1792–93 in Nationaal Archief 1.01.02 inv. 6695 filed with the clerks’ clear copies, aligned them, and rebuilt the code: a homophonic nomenclator in which the mark is part of the group (773 and 773 with a tilde are different entries), 2,385 group forms ( pull request #66 ). Applied to this letter it gives a value to 601 of the 696 groups, 142 of them tentative, and four groups spell “Maarschalk Potocki” exactly as in the despatch of 16 June 1792. The gist is Polish affairs before the Grodno Diet of 1793. But tested blind, rebuilding the code without each training letter and decoding that letter, only 60% of groups come out exactly right (70% character similarity; shuffled codes 0.3%). That is good evidence the code is the right one and not enough for a reading, so the entry stays “attempted”, now partial. WAINUT found no decipherment of this letter in the digitised inv. 6695, and the letter itself is not among that inventory’s online scans, though DECODE files it there; the Fagel archive (NA 1.10.29) and Colenbrander’s Gedenkstukken are not yet searched. Their edition and files: targets/vanreede1793/wainut/ .

The despatch is filed among the Staten-Generaal’s secret papers, addressed to the Secret Committee. DECODE gives a transcription (D3608) in which each mark is written after its digit; 696 groups, 513 distinct marked forms ( analyze_1893.py ). The marks are systematic, not slips: the same marked forms recur, and van Reede’s despatches of 1787–88 in the Grand Chiffre have none.

Known keys. The 1793 Fagel key bundle on DECODE (R2842–R2852): the pages of R2846, R2848, R2850 and R2851 were fetched and their numeric cells indexed (the other records were seen only as thumbnails, and R2852 not at all), and the cells R1893’s groups would address in R2851 were cut out and compared; the deciphered control R2243 was tried too. None gives Dutch. The 1782 Grand Chiffre (R1024) that reads van Reede’s earlier letters is another system. From the ciphertext. 513 distinct forms in 696 tokens leave most forms with one or two occurrences. A code of that size cannot be rebuilt from so little text without a crib, and none was found.

The key of the Secret Committee’s 1793 correspondence, or a deciphered copy (the Fagel archive, NA 1.10.29, is the next place to look); or a better-validated version of WAINUT’s rebuilt code, checked against the rest of the Fagel key bundle. Attempted, partial.

Reçue le 18 de decembre 1737 et répondu le 25 du mesme mois. Depuis la lettre que je vous écrivis, Monsieur, le 25 may dernier, dont je joins icy le duplicata, j’ay reçu celle que vous m’avez fait l’amitié de m’écrire le 1er avril dernier. Je sçay très bon gré au Père Hyacinte de Tours des attentions qu’il a eu pour vous ; le voyage qu’il a entrepris pour vous offrir ses services est une preuve de son bon cœur, et vous avez bien fait de tirer parti de cette demarche auprès de l’ambassadeur de Perse. Je vous envoye pour ce dernier une lettre par laquelle je le remercie des bontés qu’il a eu pour vous et je le prie de vous les continuer. Je ne pus vous l’envoyer avec ma lettre du 25 may. La situation des affaires dans ce païs est toujours fort critique ; on n’y est nullement tranquille et l’on y craint fort que l’empereur n’entre incessamment en guerre avec les Turcs. Le calme est tout à fait retabli parmi les princes chrétiens. Le Roy Stanislas est à Luneville et Mr du Theil est occupé à Vienne à dresser le traité de paix. Ce que vous pourrez nous écrire des affaires du païs Mr Otter. f143v où vous allés sera d’autant plus intéressant que les nouvelles publiques varient extrêmement à cet égard. Je vous fis conn[oistre] avant votre depart d’icy qu’il conviendroit au intérêt de la France de retablir le commerce que nous avions autrefois en Perse. Cette idée, qui ne venoit allors que de moy, me paroît avoir esté goutée par la cour et par nos ministres. Ainsi je voudrois que, dès que vous seres arrivé à Ispahan, vous sondassies le terrein et que vous travaillassies à faire insinuer à Sach Nadir le désir que le Roy auroit de renouvel[e]r les mesme liaisons d’amitié qu’il y avoit eu autrefois entre la France et la Perse. Vous pourries faire pré[s]sen[t]ir ce prince sur l’etablissement d’un consul de France à Ispahan, et si un[e] lettre de felicitation du Roy sur son avenement au trone luy seroit agréable. Je ne f144r vous pré[s]cris rien sur les moyens de faire reussir cette affaires ; vous en decideres mieux, estant sur les lieu, que je ne pourrois faire de Constantinople. Vous compties, Monsieur, de n’avoir à vous occuper dans le voyage que vous aves entrepri qu’à vous perfectionner dans la conn[oiss]ance des langues orientales. Cependant vous voyla embarqué dans la politique. Je conn[ois] assez vos talens et vos sentiments pour estre persuadé que je ne pouvois confier cette négociation en de meilleures mains. Vous deves l’estre aussi de l’attention que j’auray de faire valoir vos services dans cette occasion et de la sincerité avec laquelle je suis, Monsieur, vôtre très humble et très obéissant serviteur. Villeneuve. f145r À Constantinople le 19 aoust 1737. Il n’y a pas longtemps, Monsieur, que je vous ay écrit par duplicata et triplicata, voye d’Alep et de Bassora, pour vous donner avis que les idées que je vous avois communiquées avant vôtre départ touchant le retablissement de notre commerce en Perse ont esté goutées de la cour , qui cependant, avant que de faire aucune démarche enverss Chah Nadir, seroit bien aise d’estre informé au vrai de la situation dans laquelle il se trouve en Perse & des disposition dans lesquelle il peut estre à notre egard . J’ay reçu depuis la lettre que vous m’avez écrite d’Urfa le 24 mars, et Kerim Bey m’a fait remettre celle que vous luy aviez confiée pour moy le 26 janvier précédent. Je profite de son retour pour vous charger de nouveau, comme j’ay fait par mes précédentes, de ne rien négliger à votre arrivée à Ispahan pour sonder si Chah Nadir recevroit avec plaisir un[e] lettre de felicitation de la part du Roy sur son avenement au trone de Perse, & s’il seroit dispos[é] à permettre que nous eussions à Mr Otter. f145v l’avenir un consul à Ispahan. Le raport que vous nous faires de ce que vous aures pu decourvrir des disposition de ce prince à ce sujet doit estre accompagné d’un[e] relation exacte & circonstanciee de la situation des affaires de Perse & de quelques refflection mesme sur le tour que vous pouves prévoir qu’elle prendront, pour eviter que les demarches que [le] Roy pourroit faire en cette occasion ne nous missent en conpromis . Je suis persuadé au surplus que vous profiterés des premiers momens de loisir que vous aurés pour vous mettre en état de répondre au mémoire que je vous remis avant vôtre départ concernant notre commerce en Perse . La manière dont vous satisferés aux différens éclaircissemens que je vous ay demandés par ce mémoire ne pourra que vous faire honneur auprès des personnes qui vous protègent, et vous ne devés pas douter que je n’en fasse usage pour vôtre avancement. J’ay fait icy le plu[s] de f146r caresses que j’ay pu à Kerim Bey ; & quoique je n’aye pu avoir avec luy aucune conférence, j’ay lieu d’estre content des disposition favorables qu’il a fait paroître pour notre nation au personnes qui ont été luy parler de ma part. Il faut continuer de cultiver son amitié et luy témoigner la satisfaction que j’ay des marques qu’il m’a donné de la sienne. Je me contenteray de vous dire à l’égard des affaires de ce pays que, quoique les plé[ni]potenciaires & les médiations soient au congrés de Niemirova, les hostilites continuent de la part des Russ[e] qui ont pri Ozakou & que les imperiau qui se sont mis de la parte ont pri Nissa & se disposent au siege de Viddin. ? a été deposé & le Kiaya etranglé. On est encore incertain qui on leur donnera pour ?. Je suis très parfaitement, Monsieur, vôtre très humble et très obéissant serviteur. Villeneuve.
